x: Leroy ran his usual couple of 'stormers' to collect two seconds, clocking 22.8 in the furlong and 49.6 in the 440 yds behind international half-miler Mike Fleet of Croydon.
Dave Cocks lined up alongside such experienced men as internationals Mike Fleet and Bob Setti. On the first lap Dave's inexperience was mercilessly revealed as he trailed the field in sixth position.

After a 55 sec. first lap, Mike Fleet of Croydon A.C tore into the lead chased hard by Dave - the rest of the field being left way behind. Into the finishing straight and our man fought his way past a greatly disillusioned Fleet, who obviously had thought he would have the race all his own way.
Tony Brooks recorded his fastest 'quarter' of the season after pushing Mike Fleet (Croydon) at the half-way mark but tying up in the finishing straight.

The newly formed Organisation & Development Committee of the A.A.A. under the secretaryship of Mike Fleet, wasted no time in producing a draft plan for transforming the chaos that is our summer season into a state of highly competitive order.
